intended_object: The functorial map on finitely branching node-labelled (rose) trees: relabel every node by applying f, keeping the tree shape (from the docstring and name).
explanation: Unfolding bind on ⟨x, xs⟩ gives ⟨f x, [] ++ List.map (map f) xs⟩ = ⟨f x, List.map (map f) xs⟩. That is the standard structural map: it applies f to every label and preserves the tree shape. Leaves map correctly to ⟨f x, []⟩. The definition is fully general in A and B. As far as I know, Mathlib has no rose-tree type; its Tree is binary, so it is not the same object.
